name: ESWATINI

flag.title: Shield & Spears
flag.note: Blue, red & yellow — shield unites all

lead: Eswatini is a tiny landlocked kingdom between South Africa and Mozambique. You could drive across it in two hours, yet it packs dramatic mountains, wildlife-filled plains, and living royal culture unlike anywhere on Earth. Africa's last absolute monarchy, ruled by a king whose family has led the Swazi for 200+ years.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: Smaller than Wales or New Jersey

sections.animals: Big game in a tiny kingdom
sections.history: From Ngwane III to Mswati III

geo: Eswatini drops from cool Highveld mountains in the west — where Malolotja Falls plunge 89 metres — through lush Middleveld to hot, flat Lowveld savanna in the east. Four distinct zones in one tiny country!
The Ezulwini Valley, meaning 'Place of Heaven', holds the royal palace and parliament. Nearby, Sibebe Rock is a three-billion-year-old granite dome, one of the world's largest exposed rock faces.
animals: Hlane Royal National Park shelters white rhinos, elephants, lions, giraffes, and hippos. Rangers guard the rhinos closely, making Eswatini one of southern Africa's key rhino conservation success stories.

Eswatini is one of Africa's only breeding sites for the rare blue swallow. Over 500 bird species have been recorded here — remarkable for a nation smaller than Wales — alongside impala, kudu, and zebra.
culture: Every August, up to 40,000 unmarried girls travel nationwide for the Umhlanga Reed Dance. Each cuts a tall reed, presents it to the Queen Mother, then dances in brilliant beaded costumes — one of Africa's most spectacular gatherings.

The sacred Incwala ceremony each December renews the king's power through six days of ancient songs heard nowhere else. Swazi craftspeople are celebrated for woven baskets and vibrant hand-poured candles sold worldwide.
history: The Swazi kingdom took shape in the mid-1700s under King Ngwane III. King Mswati II later expanded it so powerfully that both country and people were named after him. British protection began in the 1890s; independence came in 1968.
In 2018, King Mswati III renamed the nation from Swaziland to Eswatini — 'Land of the Swazis' — on the 50th independence anniversary. He rules today as Africa's only remaining absolute monarch.
wows: Eswatini is Africa's last absolute monarchy — the king holds full power over every branch of government.
Sibebe Rock near Mbabane is 3 billion years old and one of Earth's largest granite domes.
Tiny Malolotja reserve is one of the only African breeding sites for the endangered blue swallow.
Eswatini is Taiwan's only diplomatic ally on the entire African continent.
The lilangeni is pegged exactly 1:1 to the South African rand — both coins spend equally.
Eswatini is Africa's 4th-biggest sugar producer despite being smaller than Wales.
The Umhlanga Reed Dance draws up to 40,000 participants — one of the continent's biggest gatherings.

myths.fact: The king renamed it Eswatini in 2018 to honour the Swazi language and shed the colonial name — though old maps still say Swaziland.
Eswatini is a fully independent sovereign kingdom with its own king, currency, and culture — South Africa simply surrounds it on three sides.
